title: Review: Stationary waves and harmonics; Total internal reflection and optical fibres; Photons and the photoelectric effect; Wave–particle duality
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: Q01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; Q03-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; Q03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W10-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: Q01-1#N.9a, Q03-1#N.16, W05-1#N.5a, W10-1#N.4a, W10-uk1#N.10, Q01-1#N.13, Q03-1#N.4a, W05-1#N.14a, W10-uk1#N.6, Q01-1#N.4c, Q03-1#N.17b, W05-1#N.3a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Planck constant
items.clue: Symbol h: the energy of one quantum of light divided by its f; 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s.

items.label: Electron diffraction
items.clue: Bright concentric rings on a fluorescent screen after a beam passes through thin graphite.

items.label: Wave–particle duality
items.clue: Idea that light and matter each need two models, and the experiment decides which one shows.

items.label: Reflection
items.clue: Bouncing back from a fixed end or pipe end, which supplies the partner moving the opposite way.

questions.stem: Predict first. Which observation from photoelectric experiments cannot be explained by the classical wave theory of light?

options.text: Photoelectrons are emitted without any measurable delay, even in very dim light.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the light is made much more intense.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the frequency of the light is raised.
Every photoelectron leaves the metal with kinetic energy exactly hf minus the work function.

questions.stem: A laser beam of power 2.0 W falls normally on a surface that absorbs all of it. What force does the beam exert on the surface? Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Each absorbed photon delivers momentum E/c, so the force is P/c = 2.0 ÷ 3.00 × 10⁸ = 6.7 × 10⁻⁹ N.

questions.stem: A glass block of refractive index 1.52 is under water of refractive index 1.33. A ray inside the glass meets the glass–water boundary at an angle of incidence of 55.0°. What happens to the ray?

options.text: It is totally internally reflected, as 55.0° is more than 41.1°.
It refracts into the water at 69.4° to the normal.
It refracts into the water at 45.8° to the normal.
It passes into the water at 55.0°, without bending.

questions.explanation: The critical angle is sin⁻¹(1.33/1.52) = 61.0°, and 55.0° < 61.0°, so it refracts: 1.52 sin 55.0° = 1.33 sin θ₂, θ₂ = 69.4°.

questions.stem: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in a standing wave. Its nodes are at x = 0, 0.40 m, 0.80 m and 1.20 m, measured from one end. Points P, Q and R on the string are at x = 0.10 m, 0.20 m and 0.70 m. Which statement about the oscillations of P, Q and R is correct?

options.text: P and Q oscillate π/4 rad out of phase, being λ/8 apart.
P and Q oscillate in phase, with amplitudes equal to each other.
P and R oscillate in antiphase, with equal amplitudes.
P and R oscillate in phase, with equal amplitudes.

questions.stem: A loudspeaker emitting a 1000 Hz note faces a hard wall. A microphone moved along the line between them detects positions of minimum loudness 0.17 m apart. What is the speed of sound?

options.text: 170 m s⁻¹
340 m s⁻¹
85 m s⁻¹
680 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Node to node = λ/2, so λ = 0.34 m. v = fλ = 1000 × 0.34 = 340 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: Light whose photons each have energy 4.0 eV shines on three metals: X, with work function 2.0 eV; Y, with work function 3.0 eV; and Z, with work function 4.5 eV. Which statement about the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted from each metal is correct?

options.text: Z's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and X's electrons the least
X's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and Z emits no electrons
All three metals emit electrons, each with the same maximum kinetic energy
Their maximum kinetic energies cannot be ranked without the light's intensity

questions.stem: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 2.0 kV. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and treat the electron as non-relativistic. What is the de Broglie wavelength of the electron?

An optical fibre has a glass core of refractive index 1.50, surrounded by glass of refractive index 1.40. On a straight stretch, a ray meets the core's wall at 75° to the normal. Where the fibre bends, the same ray meets the wall at 66° to the normal. What happens at each point?

options.text: Trapped at both: once light is inside the core, it cannot leave.
Totally internally reflected at 75°; at 66° some light passes out of the core.
Totally internally reflected at both, as both angles are more than 41.8°.
Some light passes out at 75°, but the ray is trapped at 66°.

questions.explanation: The critical angle is sin⁻¹(1.40/1.50) = 69.0°. 75° > 69.0°: TIR. 66° < 69.0°: part of the light refracts out (at 78° to the normal). A sharp bend lets light leak.

questions.stem: A tuning fork of frequency 384 Hz is held over a resonance tube. The first resonance occurs when the air column is 22.0 cm long. Ignoring any end correction, what is the speed of sound in the air?

options.text: 169 m s⁻¹
436 m s⁻¹
338 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: First resonance: L = λ/4, so λ = 4 × 0.220 = 0.880 m. v = fλ = 384 × 0.880 = 338 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A laser pointer emits light of wavelength 633 nm with a power of 5.0 mW. How many photons does it emit each second? Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
A beam of electrons and a beam of protons are each accelerated from rest through 100 V and aimed at the same crystal, whose rows of atoms are 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m apart. Which beam shows clear diffraction?

options.text: Only the protons: they are heavier, so they hit the atoms harder and are scattered more.
Both equally: they have the same charge and the same p.d., so they gain the same energy.
Only the electrons: their wavelength is comparable with the spacing of the atoms.
Neither: diffraction is a property of waves, and both beams are made of particles.

questions.stem: Light can cross a flat boundary between water (n = 1.33) and glass (n = 1.50) in either direction. Which statement about total internal reflection at this boundary is correct?

options.text: It can occur for light in the glass heading towards the water.
It can occur for light that is in the water and heading towards the glass.
It can occur for light going either way, if the angle is large enough.
It needs air beyond the boundary, so it does not occur at this one.

questions.explanation: Total internal reflection needs light heading into a lower refractive index: here, light in the glass (1.50) meeting the water (1.33), at angles of incidence above sin⁻¹(1.33/1.50), about 62°.
